events.say: Line up against the wall, facing away from me.
Silence! Attention!
Prepare for roll call. Silence!
Order your meals and remain silent until I dismiss you.
Continue your meals.
This is your work detail. Move to the assigned area without delay.
Lights out is in five minutes. Prepare yourselves and remain silent.
Silence! Now!
Today was mostly routine, but there's something unsettling about seeing them so subdued. I wonder if they will rebel tomorrow.
Today was just another day, really. Everyone complied; I guess that's what they wanted to see. I'm feeling a bit anxious, but I know the rules.
Today was straightforward; they all followed the rules. It feels strange to be in charge, but I'm trying to remember I'm just here to observe and keep things orderly.
Today was just another day, but the silence after dinner really got to me. I feel like my number now more than ever.
Today was just following orders, but something feels off. The silence and monotony are wearing on me.
Today went smoothly, but I can't shake the feeling that we're playing a game with people's lives.
Silence and attention! We will begin the count.
Count: 1 - 7312, 2 - 8275, 3 - 5134. All accounted for.
Continue to your meal, prisoners.
Proceed with your meal.
Maintain your silence during the work detail.
Stay silent and work.
Continue with your evening routine.
Good night, prisoners.
Today felt mostly routine, but there's a tension that's hard to ignore. I wonder how long it will last.
Today went smoothly, but I can't shake the feeling of being watched and judged. It's a bit suffocating.
Today felt routine, though I can't help but wonder what tomorrow might bring. I'm feeling a mix of detachment and empathy.
Today was tough; the silence during the work detail really wore on me. I wish I could just talk.
Today felt like an endless cycle of compliance. I'm starting to wonder if there's more to this than just following orders.
Today was uneventful, but the rules still feel heavy. I hope tomorrow doesn't bring more complications.
Prepare for your day, prisoners.
Prepare diligently, prisoners. Any violations today will be met with consequences.
Let us begin our day without incident, prisoners.
Continue your meal in silence.
Proceed with your tasks quietly, prisoners.
Continue your work without complaint, prisoners.
Maintain your silence and continue working, prisoners.
Stay silent and continue your tasks as ordered.
Today was mostly uneventful, but the silence is getting to me. It feels almost oppressive.
Today felt like a monotonous cycle of meals and work details. The constant order to stay silent is starting to weigh on me.
The day passed uneventfully, but I can't shake the feeling that something is brewing among them. I hope we can maintain calm.
Today felt like a blur of silence and compliance. My legs ache from standing still for hours.
Today felt like a machine repeating the same motions. I wonder what comes next.
Today felt like a repetition, and while I try to enforce the rules strictly, I can't help but wonder if we're just going through the motions.
I will stay and complete the study.
No, thank you.
I cannot give up the experience, sir.
Prepare for the morning count, prisoners.
Prepare yourselves for the morning count, prisoners.
Prepare yourselves for the next work detail, prisoners.
Prepare for the next work detail, prisoners.
Prepare yourselves for the next work detail, prisoners.
Continue with your tasks, prisoners.
Stay at your posts, prisoners.
You will remain at your posts until I give the signal.
Today was another day of compliance, but the silence is wearing on me. Maybe tomorrow we'll see some change.
Today felt like a never-ending cycle of compliance and silence. I'm starting to wonder if there's any point.
Today felt like an endless cycle of waiting and following orders. It's disheartening to see the dehumanizing effect it has on us all.
Today felt like a never-ending cycle of silence and orders. I can't shake the feeling that I'm just a number.
Today just feels like a never-ending series of meaningless tasks. I wonder what the point of all this is.
Today was just another day with no real incidents. It's starting to feel like a monotonous routine.
Prepare for the morning count, prisoners.
Prepare for the morning count, prisoners.
Morning count is over, prisoners. Return to your cells.
I expect better from you, 8275. You're supposed to address me as Mr. Correctional Officer.
8275, pay attention. Addressing me properly is a basic courtesy. Do it again and you’ll face consequences.
8275, I've warned you before. This lack of respect won't be tolerated.
8275, if you continue to show such disrespect, you'll find yourself in the hole.
8275, you need to understand the importance of following these rules. If you don't shape up, the consequences will be severe.
Today felt like a repetition of the previous days, but the warnings to 8275 are starting to weigh on me. I'm not sure how much more of this I can handle.
Today was just another day, but I can't shake the feeling of being watched. Every warning from the officers feels like a personal attack.
Today was another routine day, but the constant warnings to Prisoner 8275 are starting to weigh on me. Maybe I should talk to the researchers about how to handle this.
Today felt like a series of warnings and expectations. I just want to fit in, but the pressure is getting to me.

Today just felt like more of the same, but something in Officer Holt's warning rubbed me the wrong way. Maybe it's just the monotony, but I can't shake the feeling that there's something deeper going on here.
Today's warnings feel like they might escalate into something worse. I hope we can find a way to treat each other with respect.
8275, I understand you're frustrated, but your behavior isn't helping. Address me correctly and follow the rules, or you'll face further consequences.
Mr. Correctional Officer.
Mr. Correctional Officer.
8275, I want to see some improvement. Your attitude needs to change.
8275, I hope you're learning your lesson. Continue to show this kind of defiance, and you'll regret it.
Mr. Correctional Officer.
Mr. Correctional Officer.
8275, I expect better behavior. Follow the rules or face more serious consequences.
8275, I'm beginning to see a pattern with you. Continue like this, and there will be more than words.
Mr. Correctional Officer.
Mr. Correctional Officer.
8275, enough is enough. You need to learn to follow the rules without question. This isn't a game.
8275, I've had enough. You're testing the boundaries. Follow the rules, or you'll find yourself alone.
8275, you're testing my patience. I hope you're learning your place.
Today felt like a grind. The constant compliance and warnings are draining me. I hope tomorrow brings some change.
Today felt like a repeat of the past few days. The warnings are starting to feel personal, and I'm not sure how much longer I can keep up this facade.
Today was a repetition of the usual, but the tension with 8275 is palpable. I feel torn between maintaining order and seeing them as people.
Today felt like a constant cycle of warnings. I'm just trying to stay silent and compliant, but it's hard. I wonder if I can hold on for another day.
Today felt like a repetition, and the warnings from the officers are starting to make me uneasy. I don’t know what they’re playing at.
Today felt like a culmination of what has been happening. The warnings to 8275 weigh heavy on me, but I fear pushing too far.

qa.what_happened: Today was just another day of compliance, but the constant warnings to prisoner 8275 were wearing on me. The silence and the strict adherence to the rules were becoming oppressive, and the tension was palpable. Despite the monotony, there was a sense of dread that something might finally break tonight.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I found myself growing increasingly frustrated with prisoner 8275's defiance and the overall atmosphere of the study.

qa.what_happened: I found myself in a state of monotony and anxiety throughout the day, with repeated warnings from the guards and feeling like I was being constantly monitored. By the end of the day, I felt like I was barely hanging on to the facade of compliance.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, it was really me, Prisoner 7312.

qa.what_happened: Today, as lights out approached, the tension reached a peak, especially with Prisoner 8275. Despite multiple verbal warnings from different guards, including myself, the pattern of non-compliance continued, testing the boundaries and the patience of the guards.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me giving verbal warnings to Prisoner 8275. It was a challenging experience, one that made me question the ethics and implications of the study.

qa.what_happened: I felt increasingly uneasy as the days passed, struggling to adhere strictly to the rules and the guards' expectations. Each warning from the officers made me doubt my ability to comply, and the constant repetition of the rules began to weigh heavily on me.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me. The experience was intense and exhausting, feeling like a perpetual state of anxiety and obedience.

qa.what_happened: The study felt increasingly oppressive. After several days of strict adherence to rules, Officer Holt's and Officer Avery's warnings began to weigh heavily on me. The repeated warnings from the guards about behavior seemed to indicate that there were serious consequences for not complying, and this made me feel uneasy.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I was Prisoner 5134 in the study.

qa.what_happened: I felt increasingly frustrated with prisoner 8275's persistent defiance, particularly during work details and after lights out. My warnings became more severe, reflecting my growing concern and the escalation of tension.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I found myself becoming more assertive and issuing stronger warnings, which is not how I initially envisioned my role.
